sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 106–112)
points: Lesson 106: "Mhoro shamwari yangu. Wakafamba sei nezuro; wakasvika zvakanaka here?" — Hello my friend. How was your trip yesterday; did you arrive safely?
Lesson 107: "Ndapota huyai muchinyararire nokuti murwere achangobatwa nehope." — Please come in quietly because the patient has just fallen asleep.
Lesson 108: "Ndapota tumira mashoko acho zvakare nokuti handina kuaverenga zvakanaka." — Please send the message again because I did not read it properly.
Lesson 109: "Tiri kudzokorora zvatakadzidza nezuro tisati tanyora bvunzo." — We are reviewing what we learned yesterday before we write the exam.
Lesson 110: "Basa ranhasi rakawanda asi ndicharipedza zvishoma nezvishoma." — Today's work is a lot, but I will finish it little by little.
Lesson 111: "Baba vako vakambokutaurira nhoroondo yedzinza remhuri yenyu here?" — Has your father ever told you the history of your family's lineage?
Lesson 112: "Mwana uyu anoverenga zvakanaka uye anofarira kunyora nyaya pfupi." — This child reads well and enjoys writing short stories.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('Mhoro'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?
Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('huyai'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]
Talking About the Past ('zvakare'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Actions Happening Right Now: The '-ri ku-' Progressive: [Subject + -ri] + ku-[verb] -> Ndiri kuverenga (I am reading) | Vari kufamba (They are walking) | Mvura iri kunaya (It is raining)
Talking About the Past ('rakawanda'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('vakambokutaurira'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Following Up on a Friend's Journey ('Wakafamba Sei?'): Among friends ('shamwari'), asking 'Wakafamba sei nezuro; wakasvika zvakanaka here?' ('How did you travel yesterday; did you arrive safely?') is the standard warm follow-up the day after someone has taken an intercity bus or road trip..

Visiting the Sick ('ushanya Murwere') & Quiet Consideration: Visiting an ill relative or neighbour ('murwere') to offer comfort is a core duty in Shona culture ('kubata maoko' / 'kutarisa murwere'), and visitors enter quietly ('muchinyararire') whenever the patient has just fallen asleep ('achangobatwa nehope')..

Mobile Messaging ('Kutumira Mashoko') Across Urban & Rural Zimbabwe: SMS and WhatsApp messages ('mashoko') are the lifeblood of daily communication across Zimbabwe, connecting relatives in Harare, Bulawayo, and Mutare with family members at rural homesteads..

Group Study & Exam Revision ('Kudzokorora') in Zimbabwean Schools: Before sitting school or university examinations ('kunyora bvunzo'), Zimbabwean students frequently form study groups to review previous lessons together ('kudzokorora zvatakadzidza'), testing each other aloud..

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 16 Review — Grammar Mastery: How do you say 'Although it rained heavily, we arrived home safely'?
options: Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
Kana mvura ikanaya mangwana, hatisi kuenda kumunda.
Mvura iri kunaya kunze saka vana vari mumba.
Zuva rakabuda masikati mbatya dzikaoma nekukurumidza.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Kunyangwe' means 'although / even though', 'yakanaya' is past tense ('rained'), and 'takasvika' is 'we arrived'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 16 Review — Numbers & Colours: Which phrase means 'three white trucks and two black cars'?
options: rori chena imwe nemotokari tsvuku nhatu
marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
makombi maviri chena nemabhazi mana matema
shangu nhema mbiri nehembe tsvuku imwe
review_exercises.correct_answer: marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
review_exercises.explanation: 'Marori machena matatu' = 'three white trucks' and 'nemotokari nhema mbiri' = 'and two black cars'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 16 Review — Locatives & Existence: Which word means 'Inside the wooden bowl there are roasted caterpillars'?
options: Patafura pane mabhuku nezvinyoreso.
Kumusika kune michero nemiriwo mizhinji.
Mundiro yemuti mune madora akakangwa.
Parutivi pemugwagwa pane miti mirefu.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Mu-' ('inside') + 'ndiro yemuti' ('wooden bowl') pairs with 'mune' ('there is inside').

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 16 Review — Conditionals & Reciprocal Verbs: What does 'tikashanda nesimba tichibatsirana' mean?
options: when they finished working at the market
because he worked alone in the field
before you start writing the examination
if we work hard helping one another
review_exercises.correct_answer: if we work hard helping one another
review_exercises.explanation: 'Tikashanda nesimba' = 'if we work with strength/hard', and 'tichibatsirana' ('-an-' reciprocal suffix) = 'helping each other'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 16 Review — Cultural & Historical Vocabulary: What does the phrase 'zvivakwa zvematombo' refer to?
options: stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)
wooden handles used on farm hoes and shovels
modern traffic lights at city intersections
plastic tanks mounted beside houses to store water
review_exercises.correct_answer: stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 16 Review — Translate this new synthesis sentence into English: 'Vanhu vazhinji vari kutengesa michero nemiriwo pamusika.'
options: Our ancestors built stone walls without mortar long ago.
Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
Two women are sitting under an umbrella near the road.
We are planning to visit our grandparents next month.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Vanhu vazhinji' = 'Many people', 'vari kutengesa' = 'are selling', 'michero nemiriwo' = 'fruits and vegetables', 'pamusika' = 'at the market'.
